81: /****************************************************************************
82:  * Name: nxsched_smp_call_add

84:  * Description:
85:  *   Add call data to other processors
86:  *
87:  * Input Parameters:

89:  *   data  - Call data

96: static void nxsched_smp_call_add(int cpu,
97:                                  FAR struct smp_call_data_s *data)
98: {
99:   FAR sq_queue_t *call_queue = &g_smp_call_queue[cpu];
100:   irqstate_t flags;
101: 
102:   flags = spin_lock_irqsave(&g_smp_call_lock);
103:   if (!sq_inqueue(&data->node[cpu], call_queue))
104:     {
105:       sq_addlast(&data->node[cpu], call_queue);
106:     }
107: 
108:   spin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_smp_call_lock, flags);
109: }

175: /****************************************************************************
176:  * Name: nxsched_smp_call_handler
177:  *
178:  * Description:
179:  *   SMP function call handler
180:  *
181:  * Input Parameters:
182:  *   irq     - Interrupt id
183:  *   context - Regs context before irq
184:  *   arg     - Interrupt arg
185:  *
186:  * Returned Value:
187:  *   Result
188:  *
189:  ****************************************************************************/
190: 
191: int nxsched_smp_call_handler(int irq, FAR void *context,
192:                              FAR void *arg)
193: {
194:   FAR sq_queue_t *call_queue;
195:   FAR sq_entry_t *curr;
196:   FAR sq_entry_t *next;
197:   int cpu = this_cpu();
198: 
199:   irqstate_t flags = spin_lock_irqsave(&g_smp_call_lock);
200: 
201:   call_queue = &g_smp_call_queue[cpu];
202: 
203:   sq_for_every_safe(call_queue, curr, next)
204:     {
205:       FAR struct smp_call_data_s *data =
206:         container_of(curr, struct smp_call_data_s, node[cpu]);
207:       FAR struct smp_call_cookie_s *cookie;
208:       int ret;
209: 
210:       sq_rem(&data->node[cpu], call_queue);
211: 
212:       spin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_smp_call_lock, flags);
213: 
214:       ret = data->func(data->arg);
215: 
216:       flags = spin_lock_irqsave(&g_smp_call_lock);
217: 
218:       cookie = data->cookie;
219:       if (cookie != NULL)
220:         {
221:           if (ret < 0)
222:             {
223:               cookie->error = ret;
224:             }
225: 
226:           /* Insert ack back to original cpu call queue,
227:            * add direct avoid nxsched_smp_call_add g_smp_call_lock again.
228:            */
229: 
230: #if CONFIG_SMP_CALL_POOL_COUNT > 0
231:           sq_addlast(&cookie->ack.node[cookie->cpu],
232:                      &g_smp_call_queue[cookie->cpu]);
233:           up_send_smp_call(1 << cookie->cpu);
234: #else
235:           nxsem_post(&cookie->sem);
236: #endif
237:         }
238:     }
239: 
240:   spin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_smp_call_lock, flags);
241:   return OK;
242: }

296: /****************************************************************************
297:  * Name: nxsched_smp_call
298:  *
299:  * Description:
300:  *   Call function on multi processors, wait function callback
301:  *
302:  * Input Parameters:
303:  *   cpuset - Target cpuset
304:  *   func   - Function
305:  *   arg    - Function args
306:  *
307:  * Returned Value:
308:  *   Result
309:  *
310:  ****************************************************************************/
311: 
312: int nxsched_smp_call(cpu_set_t cpuset, nxsched_smp_call_t func,
313:                      FAR void *arg)
314: {
315:   FAR struct smp_call_cookie_s *c;
316:   int semcount;
317:   int cpucnt;
318:   int ret = OK;
319:   int i;
320: 
321: #if CONFIG_SMP_CALL_POOL_COUNT > 0
322:   c = nxsched_smp_call_cookie_alloc();
323: #else
324:   struct smp_call_cookie_s cookie;
325: 
326:   c = &cookie;
327: #endif
328: 
329:   nxsched_smp_call_cookie_init(c, func, arg);
330: 
331:   ret = nxsched_smp_call_async(cpuset, &c->req);
332: 
333:   if (ret < 0)
334:     {
335:       nxsem_destroy(&c->sem);
336:       return ret;
337:     }
338: 
339:   cpucnt = CPU_COUNT(&cpuset);
340:   if (up_interrupt_context())
341:     {
342:       /* Wait until completion. */
343: 
344:       do
345:         {
346:           nxsem_get_value(&c->sem, &semcount);
347:         }
348:       while (semcount != cpucnt);
349:     }
350:   else
351:     {
352:       for (i = 0; i < cpucnt; i++)
353:         {
354:           int rc = nxsem_wait_uninterruptible(&c->sem);
355:           if (rc < 0)
356:             {
357:               ret = rc;
358:             }
359:         }
360:     }
361: 
362:   if (c->error < 0)
363:     {
364:       ret = c->error;
365:     }
366: 
367:   nxsched_smp_call_cookie_free(c);
368:   return ret;
369: }

422: /****************************************************************************
423:  * Name: nxsched_smp_call_async
424:  *
425:  * Description:
426:  *   Call function on multi processors async
427:  *
428:  * Input Parameters:
429:  *   cpuset - Target cpuset
430:  *   data   - Call data
431:  *
432:  * Returned Value:
433:  *   Result

437: int nxsched_smp_call_async(cpu_set_t cpuset,
438:                            FAR struct smp_call_data_s *data)
439: {
440:   int cpucnt;
441:   int ret = OK;
442:   int i;
443: 
444:   /* Prevent reschedule on another processor */
445: 
446:   if (!up_interrupt_context())
447:     {
448:       sched_lock();
449:     }
450: 
451:   if (CPU_ISSET(this_cpu(), &cpuset))
452:     {
453:       ret = data->func(data->arg);
454:       if (data->cookie != NULL)
455:         {
456:           data->cookie->error = ret;
457:           nxsem_post(&data->cookie->sem);
458:           if (ret < 0)
459:             {
460:               goto out;
461:             }
462:         }
463: 
464:       CPU_CLR(this_cpu(), &cpuset);
465:     }
466: 
467:   cpucnt = CPU_COUNT(&cpuset);
468:   if (cpucnt == 0)
469:     {
470:       goto out;
471:     }
472: 
473:   for (i = 0; i < CONFIG_NCPUS; i++)
474:     {
475:       if (CPU_ISSET(i, &cpuset))
476:         {
477:           nxsched_smp_call_add(i, data);
478:           if (--cpucnt == 0)
479:             {
480:               break;
481:             }
482:         }
483:     }
484: 
485:   up_send_smp_call(cpuset);
486: 
487: out:
488:   if (!up_interrupt_context())
489:     {
490:       sched_unlock();
491:     }
492: 
493:   return ret;
494: }

75:   sched_note_start(tcb);

78:   /* wait until cpu0 in idle() */

80:   while (!OSINIT_IDLELOOP());

83:

85: 
86:   sinfo("CPU%d: Beginning Idle Loop\n", this_cpu());

97:  * Name: nx_smp_start
98:  *
99:  * Description:
100:  *   In an SMP configuration, only one CPU is initially active (CPU 0).
101:  *   System initialization occurs on that single thread. At the completion
102:  *   of the initialization of the OS, just before beginning normal
103:  *   multitasking, the additional CPUs would be started by calling this
104:  *   function.
105:  *
106:  * Input Parameters:
107:  *   None
108:  *
109:  * Returned Value:
110:  *   Zero on success; a negated errno value on failure.
111:  *
112:  * Assumption:
113:  *   Runs before the full initialization sequence has completed.  Runs after
114:  *   all OS facilities are set up, but before multi-tasking has been started.
115:  *
116:  ****************************************************************************/

118: int nx_smp_start(void)
119: {
120:   int ret;
121:   int cpu;
122: 
123:   /* Flush dcache before start other CPUs. */
124: 
125:   up_flush_dcache_all();
126: 
127:   /* Start all of the other CPUs.  CPU0 is already running. */

138:         }
139:     }

57: static void mbox_clear_errors(int cpu)
58: {
59:   uintptr_t cfg = cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_CFG : BK7258_MBOX_CH2_CFG;
60:   uint32_t config = getreg32(cfg);
61:   uint32_t errors = config & BK7258_MBOX_CFG_ERROR_STATUS;
62: 
63:   if (cpu == 0 && (errors & BK7258_MBOX_CFG_WRERR_STATUS) != 0)
64:     {
65:       g_stats.write_error++;
66:     }
67: 
68:   if (cpu == 0 && (errors & BK7258_MBOX_CFG_RDERR_STATUS) != 0)
69:     {
70:       g_stats.read_error++;
71:     }
72: 
73:   if (cpu == 0 && (errors & BK7258_MBOX_CFG_WRFULL_STATUS) != 0)
74:     {
75:       g_stats.write_full++;
76:     }
77: 
78:   if (errors != 0)
79:     {
80:       putreg32((config & BK7258_MBOX_CFG_RW_MASK) | errors, cfg);

84: static bool mbox_valid_envelope(uint8_t source, uint32_t address,
85:                                 uint32_t length)
86: {
87:   if (source != 0)
88:     {
89:       g_stats.bad_source++;
90:       mbox_trace_errors();
91:       return false;
92:     }
93: 
94:   if (length != BK7258_MB_MESSAGE_SIZE)
95:     {
96:       g_stats.bad_length++;
97:       mbox_trace_errors();
98:       return false;
99:     }
100: 
101:   if ((address & 3u) != 0 || address < BK7258_CP_RAM_START ||
102:       address > BK7258_CP_RAM_END - BK7258_MB_MESSAGE_SIZE)
103:     {
104:       g_stats.bad_address++;
105:       mbox_trace_errors();
106:       return false;
107:     }

109:   return true;

112: int bk7258_mbox_send(uint8_t destination, const uint32_t data[2])
113: {
114:   irqstate_t flags;
115:   uintptr_t status;
116:   int cpu = up_cpu_index();
117: 
118:   if (!g_mbox_ready || destination > 2 || data == NULL)
119:     {
120:       return -EINVAL;
121:     }
122: 
123: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
124:   if (cpu == 1 && (destination != 1 || data[1] != 0))
125:     {
126:       return -EPERM;
127:     }
128: #endif
129: 
130:   /* CPU1 transmits through channel 1.  Full is reported by the target's
131:    * receive FIFO status register.
132:    */
133: 
134:   status = destination == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH0_STATUS :
135:             destination == 1 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_STATUS :
136:                                BK7258_MBOX_CH2_STATUS;
137:   flags = up_irq_save();
138:   if ((getreg32(status) & 1u) != 0)
139:     {
140:       up_irq_restore(flags);
141:       return -EAGAIN;
142:     }
143: 
144:   /* TDATA0/TDATA1 are staging registers and TID commits the descriptor.
145:    * Keep raw SMP kicks and transport sends from interleaving these writes.
146:    */
147: 
148:   putreg32(data[0], cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_TDATA0 :
149:                                BK7258_MBOX_CH2_TDATA0);
150:   putreg32(data[1], cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_TDATA1 :
151:                                BK7258_MBOX_CH2_TDATA1);
152:   putreg32(destination, cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_TID :
153:                                    BK7258_MBOX_CH2_TID);
154:   up_irq_restore(flags);
155:   return OK;

158: static struct mbox_rx_descriptor *mbox_alloc_desc(void)
159: {
160:   unsigned int i;
161: 
162:   for (i = 0; i < MBOX_RX_DESC_COUNT; i++)
163:     {
164:       if (!g_rx_desc[i].used)

166:           return &g_rx_desc[i];
167:         }

173: static bool mbox_priority_message(
174:   const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *message)
175: {
176:   uint8_t control = bk7258_mb_header_ctrl(message);
177: 
178:   return (control & (BK7258_MB_CTRL_ACK_BOX | BK7258_MB_CTRL_RESET)) != 0;
179: }

181: static struct mbox_rx_descriptor *mbox_oldest_desc(bool priority)
182: {
183:   struct mbox_rx_descriptor *oldest = NULL;
184:   unsigned int i;
185: 
186:   for (i = 0; i < MBOX_RX_DESC_COUNT; i++)
187:     {
188:       struct mbox_rx_descriptor *desc = &g_rx_desc[i];
189: 
190:       if (!desc->used || mbox_priority_message(&desc->message) != priority)
191:         {
192:           continue;
193:         }
194: 
195:       if (oldest == NULL || (int32_t)(desc->order - oldest->order) < 0)
196:         {
197:           oldest = desc;
198:         }
199:     }
200: 
201:   return oldest;
202: }

204: static void mbox_process_desc(void)
205: {
206:   struct mbox_rx_descriptor *desc;
207:   int ret;
208: 
209:   /* ACK and RESET never need ACK slots.  Process them ahead of a deferred
210:    * ordinary command, then retry ordinary commands in original FIFO order.
211:    */
212: 
213:   while ((desc = mbox_oldest_desc(true)) != NULL)
214:     {
215:       g_processing_order = desc->order;
216:       ret = g_callback == NULL ? -ENOSYS : g_callback(&desc->message);
217:       g_processing_order = 0;
218:       if (ret == -EAGAIN)
219:         {
220:           g_stats.descriptor_deferred++;
221:           break;
222:         }
223: 
224:       desc->used = false;
225:     }
226: 
227:   while ((desc = mbox_oldest_desc(false)) != NULL)
228:     {
229:       g_processing_order = desc->order;
230:       ret = g_callback == NULL ? -ENOSYS : g_callback(&desc->message);
231:       g_processing_order = 0;
232:       if (ret == -EAGAIN)
233:         {
234:           break;
235:         }
236: 
237:       desc->used = false;
238:     }
239: }

241: static int bk7258_mbox_irq(int irq, void *context, void *arg)
242: {
243:   uintptr_t rdata0;
244:   uintptr_t rdata1;
245:   uintptr_t sidreg;
246:   int cpu = up_cpu_index();
247:   unsigned int budget = MBOX_IRQ_DRAIN_BUDGET;
248: 
249:   (void)irq;
250:   (void)context;
251:   (void)arg;
252: 
253:   mbox_clear_errors(cpu);
254:   if (cpu == 1 && bk7258_boottrace_secondary_stage() >=
255:                   BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_ACK &&
256:                   bk7258_boottrace_secondary_stage() <
257:                   BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX_ENTER)
258:     {
259:       bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX_ENTER);
260:     }
261:   sidreg = cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_SID : BK7258_MBOX_CH2_SID;
262:   rdata0 = cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_RDATA0 : BK7258_MBOX_CH2_RDATA0;
263:   rdata1 = cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_RDATA1 : BK7258_MBOX_CH2_RDATA1;
264: 
265:   while ((bk7258_mbox_rx_status() & 2u) == 0 && budget-- != 0)
266:     {
267:       struct mbox_rx_descriptor *desc;
268:       uint32_t address;
269:       uint32_t length;
270:       uint8_t source;
271: 
272:       if (cpu == 0)
273:         {
274:           mbox_process_desc();
275:         }
276: 
277:       desc = cpu == 0 ? mbox_alloc_desc() : NULL;
278:       if (cpu == 0 && desc == NULL)
279:         {
280:           g_stats.descriptor_full++;
281:           mbox_trace_errors();
282:           break;
283:         }
284: 
285:       source = getreg32(sidreg) & 0x0fu;
286:       address = getreg32(rdata0);
287:       length = getreg32(rdata1);
288: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
289:       if (length == 0)
290:         {
291:           if (source == (uint8_t)(2 - cpu))
292:             {
293:               if (cpu == 1 && address == BK7258_MBOX_RAW_KICK)
294:                 {
295:                   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX_RAW);
296:                 }
297: 
298:               bk7258_smp_ipi_receive(irq, context, address);
299:             }
300:           else
301:             {
302:               if (cpu == 0)
303:                 {
304:                   g_stats.bad_source++;
305:                   mbox_trace_errors();
306:                 }
307:             }
308: 
309:           continue;
310:         }
311: #endif
312: 
313:       if (cpu != 0)
314:         {
315:           continue;
316:         }
317: 
318:       if (!mbox_valid_envelope(source, address, length))
319:         {
320:           continue;
321:         }
322: 
323:       __asm__ volatile("dmb sy" ::: "memory");
324:       memcpy(&desc->message, (const void *)(uintptr_t)address,
325:              sizeof(desc->message));
326:       desc->order = ++g_rx_order;
327:       desc->used = true;
328:       g_stats.rx_messages++;
329:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(0, desc->message.header);
330:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(1, address);
331:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(2, g_stats.rx_messages);
332:       mbox_process_desc();
333:     }
334: 
335:   if (cpu == 0)
336:     {
337:       mbox_process_desc();
338:     }
339: 
340:   if (cpu == 1 && bk7258_boottrace_secondary_stage() ==
341:                   BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX_RAW)
342:     {
343:       bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX_EXIT);
344:     }
345: 
346:   return OK;
347: }

391: int bk7258_mbox_init(void)
392: {
393:   int ret;
394: 
395:   if (g_mbox_ready)
396:     {
397:       return OK;
398:     }
399: 
400:   memset(g_rx_desc, 0, sizeof(g_rx_desc));
401:   g_rx_order = 0;
402:   g_processing_order = 0;
403:   memset(&g_stats, 0, sizeof(g_stats));
404: 
405:   /* CPU1 owns channel 1 and FIFO entries 2..4.  Install the callback and
406:    * descriptors before enabling the route; pre-existing FIFO entries are
407:    * then processed normally instead of being blindly discarded.
408:    */
409: 
410:   putreg32(2u | BK7258_MBOX_CFG_INT_EN | BK7258_MBOX_CFG_WRERR_EN |
411:             BK7258_MBOX_CFG_RDERR_EN | BK7258_MBOX_CFG_WRFULL_EN,
412:             BK7258_MBOX_CH1_CFG);
413:   putreg32(1u | (3u << 1), BK7258_MBOX_CH1_FIFO_CFG);
414: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
415:   putreg32(5u | BK7258_MBOX_CFG_INT_EN | BK7258_MBOX_CFG_WRERR_EN |
416:             BK7258_MBOX_CFG_RDERR_EN | BK7258_MBOX_CFG_WRFULL_EN,
417:             BK7258_MBOX_CH2_CFG);
418:   putreg32(1u | (3u << 1), BK7258_MBOX_CH2_FIFO_CFG);
419: #endif
420:   modifyreg32(BK7258_MBOX_CTRL, 0, 1u << 2);
421:   mbox_clear_errors(0);
422: 
423:   ret = irq_attach(BK7258_IRQ_MAILBOX, bk7258_mbox_irq, NULL);
424:   if (ret < 0)
425:     {
426:       return ret;
427:     }
428: 
429:   g_mbox_ready = true;
430: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
431:   g_mbox_smp_ready = true;
432: #endif
433:   modifyreg32(BK7258_CPU1_IRQ_EN1, 0, 1u << 31);
434:   up_enable_irq(BK7258_IRQ_MAILBOX);
435:   return OK;
436: }

442: #else
443:   return false;
444: #endif

31: {
32:   uintptr_t regaddr;
33:   uint32_t bit;
34:   int cpu = up_cpu_index();

36: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP

44:     {

46:       bit = 1u << extirq;

48:   else

50:       regaddr = cpu == 0 ? BK7258_CPU1_IRQ_EN1 : BK7258_CPU2_IRQ_EN1;
51:       bit = 1u << (extirq - 32);
52:     }
53: 
54:   if (enable)
55:     {
56:       modifyreg32(regaddr, 0, bit);
57:     }
58:   else

70: 
71:   for (i = 0; i < BK7258_EXTIRQ_COUNT; i += 32)
72:     {

74:       putreg32(0xffffffffu, NVIC_IRQ_CLRPEND(i));

78:   putreg32(0, BK7258_CPU2_IRQ_EN1);
79:   putreg32(0, NVIC_SYSTICK_CTRL);

81:   putreg32(DEFPRIORITY32, NVIC_SYSH4_7_PRIORITY);
82:   putreg32(DEFPRIORITY32, NVIC_SYSH8_11_PRIORITY);
83:   putreg32(DEFPRIORITY32, NVIC_SYSH12_15_PRIORITY);
84: 
85:   priority_registers = ((getreg32(NVIC_ICTR) & 0x1f) + 1) * 8;
86:   regaddr = NVIC_IRQ0_3_PRIORITY;
87:   while (priority_registers-- > 0)

94:   modifyreg32(NVIC_SYSHCON, 0,
95:               NVIC_SYSHCON_MEMFAULTENA | NVIC_SYSHCON_BUSFAULTENA |
96:               NVIC_SYSHCON_USGFAULTENA | NVIC_SYSHCON_SECUREFAULTENA);

100: static int bk7258_irqinfo(int irq, uintptr_t *regaddr, uint32_t *bit,
101:                           uintptr_t offset)
102: {
103:   int extirq;
104: 
105:   DEBUGASSERT(irq >= BK7258_IRQ_NMI && irq < NR_IRQS);
106: 
107:   if (irq >= BK7258_IRQ_FIRST)
108:     {
109:       extirq = irq - BK7258_IRQ_FIRST;
110:       *regaddr = NVIC_IRQ_ENABLE(extirq) + offset;
111:       *bit = 1u << (extirq & 31);
112:       return OK;
113:     }
114: 
115:   *regaddr = NVIC_SYSHCON;
116:   switch (irq)
117:     {
118:       case BK7258_IRQ_MEMFAULT:
119:         *bit = NVIC_SYSHCON_MEMFAULTENA;
120:         break;
121:       case BK7258_IRQ_BUSFAULT:
122:         *bit = NVIC_SYSHCON_BUSFAULTENA;
123:         break;
124:       case BK7258_IRQ_USAGEFAULT:
125:         *bit = NVIC_SYSHCON_USGFAULTENA;
126:         break;
127:       case BK7258_IRQ_SECUREFAULT:
128:         *bit = NVIC_SYSHCON_SECUREFAULTENA;
129:         break;
130:       case BK7258_IRQ_SYSTICK:
131:         *regaddr = NVIC_SYSTICK_CTRL;
132:         *bit = NVIC_SYSTICK_CTRL_ENABLE;
133:         break;
134:       default:
135:         return ERROR;
136:     }
137: 
138:   return OK;
139: }

142: {

145:   regval |= priority << NVIC_SYSH_PRIORITY_PR11_SHIFT;
146:   putreg32(regval, NVIC_SYSH8_11_PRIORITY);

160:   putreg32(0, BK7258_CPU1_IRQ_EN0);
161:   putreg32(0, BK7258_CPU1_IRQ_EN1);

163:   putreg32(DEFPRIORITY32, NVIC_SYSH4_7_PRIORITY);
164:   putreg32(DEFPRIORITY32, NVIC_SYSH8_11_PRIORITY);
165:   putreg32(DEFPRIORITY32, NVIC_SYSH12_15_PRIORITY);

172:       regaddr += 4;
173:     }

175:   irq_attach(BK7258_IRQ_SVCALL, arm_svcall, NULL);
176:   irq_attach(BK7258_IRQ_HARDFAULT, arm_hardfault, NULL);
177:   irq_attach(BK7258_IRQ_MEMFAULT, arm_memfault, NULL);
178:   irq_attach(BK7258_IRQ_BUSFAULT, arm_busfault, NULL);
179:   irq_attach(BK7258_IRQ_USAGEFAULT, arm_usagefault, NULL);
180:   irq_attach(BK7258_IRQ_SECUREFAULT, arm_securefault, NULL);
181:   arm_enable_dbgmonitor();
182:   irq_attach(BK7258_IRQ_DBGMONITOR, arm_dbgmonitor, NULL);
183: 
184:   bk7258_prioritize_svcall(NVIC_SYSH_SVCALL_PRIORITY);
185:   up_enable_irq(BK7258_IRQ_MEMFAULT);
186:   up_enable_irq(BK7258_IRQ_BUSFAULT);
187:   up_enable_irq(BK7258_IRQ_USAGEFAULT);

226:         }

65:   enum task_deliver_e priority;
66:   irqstate_t flags;

72:   per_cpu_var_smp(g_delivertasks, cpu) = SWITCH_NONE;

74:   if (priority != SWITCH_NONE &&

8: #define MBOX0_CHN0_FIFO_LEN     2
9: #define MBOX0_CHN1_FIFO_LEN     3
10: #define MBOX0_CHN2_FIFO_LEN     3
11: #else //#if CONFIG_SOC_SMP
12: #define MBOX0_CHN0_FIFO_LEN     2
13: #define MBOX0_CHN1_FIFO_LEN     4
14: #define MBOX0_CHN2_FIFO_LEN     2
15: #endif //#if CONFIG_SOC_SMP
16: 
17: #define MBOX0_CHN0_FIFO_START     0
18: #define MBOX0_CHN1_FIFO_START     (MBOX0_CHN0_FIFO_START + MBOX0_CHN0_FIFO_LEN)
19: #define MBOX0_CHN2_FIFO_START     (MBOX0_CHN1_FIFO_START + MBOX0_CHN1_FIFO_LEN)
20: 
21: //struct mbox0_fifo_cfg_t:
22: #define MBOX0_FIFO_CFG_TABLE   \
23: {   \
24: 	{MBOX0_CHN0_FIFO_START, MBOX0_CHN0_FIFO_LEN}, \
25: 	{MBOX0_CHN1_FIFO_START, MBOX0_CHN1_FIFO_LEN}, \
26: 	{MBOX0_CHN2_FIFO_START, MBOX0_CHN2_FIFO_LEN}, \
27: }
28: 
29: 
30: static mbox0_dev_t       mbox0_dev;
31: static u8                mbox0_init = 0;
32: 
33: static const mbox0_fifo_cfg_t  fifo_cfg[] = MBOX0_FIFO_CFG_TABLE;
34: 	
35: static int mbox0_drv_recieve_message(mbox0_message_t* message)
36: {
37: 	return mbox0_dev.chn_drv[SELF_CHNL]->chn_recv(&mbox0_dev.hal, message);
38: }
39: 
40: static void mbox0_drv_isr_handler(void)
41: {
42: 	uint32_t int_status;
43: 	uint32_t fifo_status;
44: 	mbox0_message_t message;
45: 
46: 	int_status = mbox0_dev.chn_drv[SELF_CHNL]->chn_get_int_status(&mbox0_dev.hal);
47: 
48: 	if(int_status == 0)
49: 		return;
50: 
51: 	do
52: 	{
53: 		fifo_status = mbox0_dev.chn_drv[SELF_CHNL]->chn_get_rx_fifo_stat(&mbox0_dev.hal);
54: 		
55: 		if(fifo_status & RX_FIFO_STAT_NOT_EMPTY)
56: 		{
57: 			mbox0_drv_recieve_message(&message);
58: 
59: 			if(message.data[1] != 0)  /* message data len is not 0. */
60: 			{
61: 				if(mbox0_dev.rx_callback != NULL)
62: 					mbox0_dev.rx_callback(&message);
63: 			}
64: 			else
65: 			{
66: 				#if CONFIG_SOC_SMP
67: 				extern void crosscore_smp_cmd_handler(uint8_t src_core, uint32_t cmd);
68: 				
69: 				crosscore_smp_cmd_handler(message.src_cpu, message.data[0]);
70: 				#endif
71: 			}
72: 		}
73: 		else
74: 		{
75: 			break;
76: 		}
77: 	} while(1);
78: 	
79: }
80: 
81: int mbox0_drv_get_send_stat(uint32_t dest_cpu, uint32_t *fifo_status)
82: {
83: 	if((dest_cpu >= MBOX_CHNL_NUM) || (fifo_status == NULL))
84: 	{
85: 		return MBOX0_HAL_SW_PARAM_ERR;
86: 	}
87: 
88: 	*fifo_status = mbox0_dev.chn_drv[dest_cpu]->chn_get_rx_fifo_stat(&mbox0_dev.hal);
89: 
90: 	return MBOX0_HAL_OK;
91: }

96: }

99: {

101: 
102: 	return 0;
103: }
104: 
105: int mbox0_init_on_current_core(int id)
106: {
107: 	int int_src = INT_SRC_MAILBOX;
108: 
109: 	if(CPU0_CORE_ID == id)
110: 	{
111: 		mbox0_hal_dev_init(&mbox0_dev.hal);  /* can only be initialized by CPU0. */
112: 		mbox0_hal_set_reg_0x2_chn_pro_disable(&mbox0_dev.hal, 1); /* channel unprotect */
113: 
114: 		for(int i = 0; i < ARRAY_SIZE(fifo_cfg); i++)
115: 			mbox0_dev.chn_drv[i]->chn_cfg_fifo(&mbox0_dev.hal, fifo_cfg[i].start, fifo_cfg[i].len);
116: 	}
117: 
118: 	mbox0_dev.chn_drv[id]->chn_int_enable(&mbox0_dev.hal, 1);
119: 
120: 	/* clear/empty RX FIFO. */
121: 	while(1)
122: 	{
123: 		mbox0_message_t message;
124: 
125: 		uint32_t fifo_status = mbox0_dev.chn_drv[id]->chn_get_rx_fifo_stat(&mbox0_dev.hal);
126: 		
127: 		if(fifo_status & RX_FIFO_STAT_NOT_EMPTY)
128: 		{
129: 			mbox0_drv_recieve_message(&message);
130: 		}
131: 		else
132: 		{
133: 			break;
134: 		}
135: 	}
136: 
137: #if CONFIG_SOC_SMP
138: 	/* enable system interrupt, every channel is hard-bound to a processor */
139: 	sys_drv_core_intr_group2_enable(id, (1 << (int_src - 32)));
140: #else
141: 	sys_drv_int_group2_enable(1 << (int_src - 32));
142: #endif
143: 
144: 	return 0;
145: }
146: 
147: int mbox0_drv_init(void)
148: {
149: 	if(mbox0_init == 1)
150: 		return 0;
151: 
152: 	mbox0_dev.chn_drv[0] = &hal_chn0_drv;
153: 	mbox0_dev.chn_drv[1] = &hal_chn1_drv;
154: 	mbox0_dev.chn_drv[2] = &hal_chn2_drv;
155: 
156: 	mbox0_dev.rx_callback = NULL;
157: 
158: 	mbox0_hal_init(&mbox0_dev.hal);
159: 
160: 	int int_src = INT_SRC_MAILBOX;
161: 
162: 	bk_int_isr_register(int_src, mbox0_drv_isr_handler, NULL);
163: 
164: #if CONFIG_SOC_SMP
165: 	mbox0_init_on_current_core(CPU1_CORE_ID);
166: 	mbox0_init_on_current_core(CPU2_CORE_ID);
167: #else
168: 	mbox0_init_on_current_core(SELF_CHNL);
169: #endif
170: 
171: 	mbox0_init = 1;
172: 
173: 	return 0;
174: }
175: 
176: int mbox0_drv_deinit(void)
177: {
178: 	if(mbox0_init == 0)
179: 		return 0;
180: 
181: 	uint8_t int_src = INT_SRC_MAILBOX;
182: 
183: 	// sys_drv_int_group2_disable(1 << (int_src - 32));
184: 
185: #if CONFIG_SOC_SMP
186: 	/* disable system interrupt, every channel is hard-bound to a processor */
187: 	sys_drv_core_intr_group2_disable(CPU0_CORE_ID, (1 << (int_src - 32)));
188: 	
189: 	/* disable system interrupt, every channel is hard-bound to a processor */
190: 	sys_drv_core_intr_group2_disable(CPU1_CORE_ID, (1 << (int_src - 32)));
191: 
192: 	mbox0_dev.chn_drv[CPU1_CORE_ID]->chn_int_enable(&mbox0_dev.hal, 0);
193: 	mbox0_dev.chn_drv[CPU2_CORE_ID]->chn_int_enable(&mbox0_dev.hal, 0);
194: #else
195: 	sys_drv_int_group2_disable(1 << (int_src - 32));
196: 	mbox0_dev.chn_drv[SELF_CHNL]->chn_int_enable(&mbox0_dev.hal, 0);
197: #endif
198: 
199: 	bk_int_isr_unregister(int_src);
200: 
201: #if CONFIG_SOC_SMP
202: 	mbox0_hal_dev_deinit(&mbox0_dev.hal);  /* can only be de-initialized by CPU0. */
203: #else
204: 	if(SELF_CHNL == 0)
205: 		mbox0_hal_dev_deinit(&mbox0_dev.hal);  /* can only be de-initialized by CPU0. */
206: #endif
207: 
208: 	mbox0_hal_deinit(&mbox0_dev.hal);
209: 	
210: 	mbox0_dev.rx_callback = NULL;
211: 
212: 	mbox0_init = 0;
213: 
214: 	return 0;
215: }

469:

471:

473:

477:

488:   /* Get the lock, end counting busy-waiting */
489:

491:

493: 
494:   sched_note_spinlock(lock, NOTE_SPINLOCK_LOCKED);
495:

230:  * algorithm (shared memory) to implement spinlock protection between AP and CP.
231:     ________________________________________
232:     1. Objectives
233:     • SMP CP/AP share a section of SRAM (fixed address), when any subsystem enters exception:
234:     o First arrival monopolizes UART → DUMP system info → direct reboot (without releasing lock);
235:     o Later arrival waits permanently (WFE()), avoiding UART conflicts.
236:     • Ensure reliable fallback solution even when shared area is corrupted.
237: 
238:     ________________________________________
239:     2. Shared memory layout (fixed address macros)
240:     • MAGIC_BEGIN / MAGIC_END: Header/tail magic numbers for validating shared area legitimacy.
241:     • CP_EXCEPTION_STATUS / AP_EXCEPTION_STATUS: Peterson's want[0]/want[1].
242:     • EXCEPTION_TURN: turn in Peterson algorithm.
243:     • EXCEPTION_DUMPER: marks who holds the lock (0=CP, 1=AP, -1=none); also used for "first come first serve DUMP" in fallback.
244:     ________________________________________
245: 
246:  */
247: 
248: /* ================= Utility functions ================= */
249: static inline void dmb_ish(void){ __asm volatile("dmb ish" ::: "memory"); }
250: static inline void cpu_wfe(void){ __asm volatile("wfe" ::: "memory"); }
251: static inline void cpu_sev(void){ __asm volatile("sev" ::: "memory"); }

253: /* ================= Validation / Repair ================= */
254: static inline int values_sane(void){
255:     uint32_t w_cp = FIXED_ADDR_CP_EXCEPTION_STATUS;
256:     uint32_t w_ap = FIXED_ADDR_AP_EXCEPTION_STATUS;
257:     uint32_t turn = FIXED_ADDR_EXCEPTION_TURN;
258:     uint32_t  dump = FIXED_ADDR_EXCEPTION_DUMPER;
259:     if (!((w_cp==0u || w_cp==1u) && (w_ap==0u || w_ap==1u))) return 0;
260:     if (!(turn==0u || turn==1u)) return 0;
261:     if (!(dump== TRAP_DEFAULT_DUMPER || dump==0 || dump==1)) return 0;
262:     return 1;
263: }

267:     if (FIXED_ADDR_EXCEPTION_MAGIC_BEGIN != TRAP_DEFAULT_MAGIC_HEAD) return 0;
268:     if (FIXED_ADDR_EXCEPTION_MAGIC_END   != TRAP_DEFAULT_MAGIC_TAIL) return 0;
269:     if (!values_sane()) return 0;
270:     return 1;
271: }
272: static inline int shared_repair(void){
273:     /* Re-seal header/tail + clear key fields (write header→clear values→write tail), with memory barrier for visibility */
274:     FIXED_ADDR_EXCEPTION_MAGIC_BEGIN = TRAP_DEFAULT_MAGIC_HEAD;
275:     dmb_ish();
276:     FIXED_ADDR_CP_EXCEPTION_STATUS = 0u;
277:     FIXED_ADDR_AP_EXCEPTION_STATUS = 0u;
278:     FIXED_ADDR_EXCEPTION_TURN      = 0u;

280:     dmb_ish();

328: /* ================= Peterson lock (volatile + DMB, symmetric) ================= */
329: static inline void peterson_lock(unsigned me){
330:     unsigned other = (me ^ 1u);
331:     FIXED_ADDR_AP_EXCEPTION_STATUS = 1u;               /* I want to enter */
332:     FIXED_ADDR_EXCEPTION_TURN = other;/* Give priority to the other */
333:     dmb_ish();                        /* Flush write buffer + establish ordering */
334:     while ((FIXED_ADDR_CP_EXCEPTION_STATUS == 1u) && (FIXED_ADDR_EXCEPTION_TURN == other)){
335:         cpu_wfe();                    /* Wait for the other to yield/exit */
336:     }
337:     /* Enter critical section */
338: }
339: /* ================= Fallback (current CPU directly DUMP; other core waits permanently) ================= */
340: static inline void fallback_take_and_dump(unsigned me){
341:     /* Grab fallback ownership: write DUMPER as me; if read back is not me, other side got it first → wait permanently */
342:     FIXED_ADDR_EXCEPTION_DUMPER = me;
343:     dmb_ish();
344:     if (FIXED_ADDR_EXCEPTION_DUMPER != me){
345:         for(;;) cpu_wfe();            /* Avoid UART conflicts */
346:     }
347: }
348: /* ================= Unified exception handling (shared by both cores) ================= */
349: static void exception_get_peterson_lock(unsigned me /*CP_ID/AP_ID*/){
350:     __disable_irq();
351:     dmb_ish();
352:     /* Shared area corrupted/uninitialized → try to repair; if repair fails → fallback (current core directly DUMP, other core waits) */
353:     if (!shared_valid()){
354:         if (!shared_repair()){
355:             fallback_take_and_dump(me);
356:         } else {
357:             /* Normal path: Peterson mutual exclusion enter exception critical section */
358:             peterson_lock(me);
359:             /* Declare me as critical section holder (also used as fallback placeholder reuse, no additional field) */
360:             FIXED_ADDR_EXCEPTION_DUMPER = me;
361:         }
362:     } else {
363:         /* Normal path: Peterson mutual exclusion enter exception critical section */
364:         peterson_lock(me);
365:         /* Declare me as critical section holder (also used as fallback placeholder reuse, no additional field) */
366:         FIXED_ADDR_EXCEPTION_DUMPER = me;
367:     }
368: 
369:     dmb_ish();
370:     cpu_sev(); /* Wake up the other side to make it quickly stuck in the waiting loop */
371: }

    389:

    按照新的架构设计, Bk7258支持双核SMP架构, 这两个核共享所有的外设以及内存资源。每个core又各自含有自身的NVIC、cache等私有资源。核间可以通过mailbox交互必要的信息。

    405:

    从内核的视角看, 采用的是逻辑id, 即不管实际在什么物理核上, 总是按0、1这样排列;

    406:

    而从应用层的视角, 由于某些配置的资源需要与具体的物理核绑定, 所以获取到的是物理id。通过os.h文件中的rtos_get_core_id()来得到。该接口返回值为1或者2, 代表物理的CPU1或CPU2。

    407:

    在SMP启动过程中, 每个core会分别将自身的core id记录到特定位置。

    注意: 上层只允许调用rtos_get_core_id()来获取core id,返回值为CPU1_CORE_ID或CPU2_CORE_ID, 对应物理CPU1和CPU2。

    SMP启动流程

    415:

    在系统的引导和初始化阶段, 只有一个上下文, 只能由一个处理器来处理。

    416:

    所以对于SMP系统, 一般会有一个先启动的core(称为primary core), 由其负责初始化整个系统的资源, 而其他的core则等待这些资源准备好后再开始工作。

23: #define BK7258_IPI_CALL         (1u << 1)
24: #define BK7258_BOOT_RETRY_LIMIT 1024
25: 
26: #define BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_NOTIFY (BK7258_MBOX_RAW_KICK + 1u)
27: #define BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_PING   (BK7258_MBOX_RAW_KICK + 2u)
28: #define BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_ACK    (BK7258_MBOX_RAW_KICK + 3u)

31: #define BK7258_BOOT_SEEN_ACK    (1u << 1)

33: #define BK7258_IPI_TRACE_ENTRY  0xb1000000u
34: #define BK7258_IPI_TRACE_CLAIM  0xb2000000u
35: #define BK7258_IPI_TRACE_SENT   0xb3000000u
36: #define BK7258_IPI_TRACE_FAIL   0xb4000000u

38: static atomic_t g_ipi_pending[CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS];
39: static atomic_t g_ipi_kicked[CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS];
40: static atomic_t g_boot_ping_received;
41: static atomic_t g_secondary_ready;

52: static int bk7258_smp_boot_send(int cpu, uint32_t command)
53: {
54:   uint32_t data[2] = {command, 0};
55:   int retry;
56: 
57:   UP_DMB();
58:   for (retry = 0; retry < BK7258_BOOT_RETRY_LIMIT; retry++)
59:     {
60:       int ret = bk7258_mbox_send((uint8_t)(cpu + 1), data);
61: 
62:       if (ret == OK)
63:         {
64:           return OK;
65:         }
66: 
67:       if (ret != -EAGAIN)
68:         {
69:           return ret;
70:         }
71: 
72:       __asm__ volatile("nop");
73:     }
74: 
75:   return -ETIMEDOUT;
76: }

78: static int bk7258_smp_kick(int cpu, uint32_t pending)
79: {
80:   uint32_t data[2] = {BK7258_MBOX_RAW_KICK, 0};
81:   int expected = 0;
82:   uint32_t retry = 0;
83: 
84:   if ((unsigned int)cpu >= CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS || cpu == this_cpu())
85:     {
86:       return -EINVAL;
87:     }
88: 
89:   bk7258_smp_trace(BK7258_IPI_TRACE_ENTRY | (pending & 0xffu));
90:   atomic_or_release(&g_ipi_pending[cpu], pending);
91:   if (!atomic_cmpxchg_acquire(&g_ipi_kicked[cpu], &expected, 1))
92:     {
93:       bk7258_smp_trace(BK7258_IPI_TRACE_CLAIM | 0x100u);
94:       return OK;
95:     }
96: 
97:   bk7258_smp_trace(BK7258_IPI_TRACE_CLAIM | (cpu & 0xffu));
98:   UP_DMB();
99:   for (;;)
100:     {
101:       int ret = bk7258_mbox_send((uint8_t)(cpu + 1), data);
102: 
103:       if (ret == OK)
104:         {
105:           bk7258_smp_trace(BK7258_IPI_TRACE_SENT | (retry & 0xffffu));
106:           return OK;
107:         }
108: 
109:       if (ret != -EAGAIN)
110:         {
111:           atomic_set_release(&g_ipi_kicked[cpu], 0);
112:           bk7258_smp_trace(BK7258_IPI_TRACE_FAIL |
113:                            ((uint32_t)(-ret) & 0xffffu));
114:           return ret;
115:         }
116: 
117:       retry++;
118:       __asm__ volatile("nop");
119:     }
120: }

122: void bk7258_smp_ipi_receive(int irq, void *context, uint32_t command)
123: {
124:   int cpu = this_cpu();
125: 
126:   if (command == BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_NOTIFY)
127:     {
128:       if (cpu == 0)
129:         {
130:           g_boot_seen |= BK7258_BOOT_SEEN_NOTIFY;
131:         }
132: 
133:       return;
134:     }
135: 
136:   if (command == BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_PING)
137:     {
138:       if (cpu == 1)
139:         {
140:           atomic_set_release(&g_boot_ping_received, 1);
141:           if (bk7258_boottrace_secondary_stage() <
142:               BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_ACK)
143:             {
144:               bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_ACK);
145:             }
146:         }
147: 
148:       return;
149:     }
150: 
151:   if (command == BK7258_MBOX_BOOT_ACK)
152:     {
153:       if (cpu == 0)
154:         {
155:           g_boot_seen |= BK7258_BOOT_SEEN_ACK;
156:         }
157: 
158:       return;
159:     }
160: 
161:   if (command != BK7258_MBOX_RAW_KICK)
162:     {
163:       return;
164:     }
165: 
166:   for (;;)
167:     {
168:       uint32_t pending = atomic_xchg_acquire(&g_ipi_pending[cpu], 0);
169: 
170:       if ((pending & BK7258_IPI_CALL) != 0)
171:         {
172:           nxsched_smp_call_handler(irq, context, NULL);
173:         }
174: 
175:       if ((pending & BK7258_IPI_SCHED) != 0)
176:         {
177:           nxsched_process_delivered(cpu);
178:         }
179: 
180:       atomic_set_release(&g_ipi_kicked[cpu], 0);
181:       UP_DMB();
182:       if (atomic_read_acquire(&g_ipi_pending[cpu]) == 0)
183:         {
184:           break;
185:         }
186: 
187:       atomic_set_release(&g_ipi_kicked[cpu], 1);
188:     }
189: }

191: int up_send_smp_sched(int cpu)
192: {
193:   int ret = bk7258_smp_kick(cpu, BK7258_IPI_SCHED);
194: 
195:   if (ret < 0)
196:     {
197:       return ret;
198:     }
199: 
200:   return ret;
201: }

203: void up_send_smp_call(cpu_set_t cpuset)
204: {
205:   int cpu;
206: 
207:   for (; cpuset != 0; cpuset &= ~(1u << cpu))
208:     {
209:       cpu = ffs((int)cpuset) - 1;
210:       if (cpu != this_cpu() && bk7258_smp_kick(cpu, BK7258_IPI_CALL) < 0)
211:         {
212:           PANIC();
213:         }
214:     }
215: }

218: {

223:       atomic_set(&g_ipi_pending[cpu], 0);
224:       atomic_set(&g_ipi_kicked[cpu], 0);

227:   g_boot_seen = 0;
228:   atomic_set(&g_boot_ping_received, 0);

112: int bk7258_mbox_send(uint8_t destination, const uint32_t data[2])
113: {
114:   irqstate_t flags;
115:   uintptr_t status;
116:   int cpu = up_cpu_index();
117: 
118:   if (!g_mbox_ready || destination > 2 || data == NULL)
119:     {
120:       return -EINVAL;
121:     }
122: 
123: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
124:   if (cpu == 1 && (destination != 1 || data[1] != 0))
125:     {
126:       return -EPERM;
127:     }
128: #endif
129: 
130:   /* CPU1 transmits through channel 1.  Full is reported by the target's
131:    * receive FIFO status register.
132:    */
133: 
134:   status = destination == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH0_STATUS :
135:             destination == 1 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_STATUS :
136:                                BK7258_MBOX_CH2_STATUS;
137:   flags = up_irq_save();
138:   if ((getreg32(status) & 1u) != 0)
139:     {
140:       up_irq_restore(flags);
141:       return -EAGAIN;
142:     }
143: 
144:   /* TDATA0/TDATA1 are staging registers and TID commits the descriptor.
145:    * Keep raw SMP kicks and transport sends from interleaving these writes.
146:    */
147: 
148:   putreg32(data[0], cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_TDATA0 :
149:                                BK7258_MBOX_CH2_TDATA0);
150:   putreg32(data[1], cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_TDATA1 :
151:                                BK7258_MBOX_CH2_TDATA1);
152:   putreg32(destination, cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_TID :
153:                                    BK7258_MBOX_CH2_TID);
154:   up_irq_restore(flags);
155:   return OK;
156: }

204: static void mbox_process_desc(void)
205: {
206:   struct mbox_rx_descriptor *desc;
207:   int ret;
208: 
209:   /* ACK and RESET never need ACK slots.  Process them ahead of a deferred
210:    * ordinary command, then retry ordinary commands in original FIFO order.
211:    */
212: 
213:   while ((desc = mbox_oldest_desc(true)) != NULL)
214:     {
215:       g_processing_order = desc->order;
216:       ret = g_callback == NULL ? -ENOSYS : g_callback(&desc->message);
217:       g_processing_order = 0;
218:       if (ret == -EAGAIN)
219:         {
220:           g_stats.descriptor_deferred++;
221:           break;
222:         }
223: 
224:       desc->used = false;
225:     }
226: 
227:   while ((desc = mbox_oldest_desc(false)) != NULL)
228:     {
229:       g_processing_order = desc->order;
230:       ret = g_callback == NULL ? -ENOSYS : g_callback(&desc->message);
231:       g_processing_order = 0;
232:       if (ret == -EAGAIN)
233:         {
234:           break;
235:         }
236: 
237:       desc->used = false;
238:     }

17: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_REENTER     0xa2000000u
18: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_OWNER_BUSY  0xa3000000u
19: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_INTENT      0xa4000000u
20: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_CONFLICT    0xa5000000u
21: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_ACQUIRED    0xa6000000u
22: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_UNLOCK      0xa7000000u
23: #define BK7258_GATE_TRACE_RELEASED    0xa8000000u
24: 
25: struct bk7258_atomic_gate_s
26: {
27:   volatile uint32_t interested[2];
28:   volatile uint32_t turn;
29:   volatile uint32_t owner;
30:   volatile uint32_t depth;
31: };
32: 
33: static struct bk7258_atomic_gate_s g_bk7258_atomic_gate
34:   __attribute__((section(".bk_spinlock"), aligned(32)));
35: 
36: static inline void bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(unsigned int cpu, uint32_t value)
37: {
38:   if (cpu == 0 && (bk7258_boottrace_words()[6] & 0xffu) == 2u)
39:     {
40:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(4, value);
41:     }
42: }
43: 
44: static bool bk7258_hwspinlock_trylock(struct hwspinlock_dev_s *dev)
45: {
46:   unsigned int cpu = (unsigned int)up_cpu_index();
47:   unsigned int other = cpu ^ 1u;
48: 
49:   (void)dev;
50:   DEBUGASSERT(cpu < 2);
51:   bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_ENTRY);
52: 
53:   /* BK7258 has only two SRAM exclusive monitors while CP, AP CPU1 and AP
54:    * CPU2 are all active.  Keep the AP-only atomic gate independent of
55:    * LDAEX/STREX so CP traffic cannot starve an AP exclusive sequence.
56:    */
57: 
58:   /* libc atomics are normally short, but the scheduler's recursive critical
59:    * section can issue another atomic operation on the same CPU.  Re-entry
60:    * must be decided before entering Peterson arbitration; otherwise a waiter
61:    * on the other CPU can make the current owner wait for itself.
62:    */
63: 
64:   if (g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner == cpu + 1u)
65:     {
66:       if (g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth == UINT32_MAX)
67:         {
68:           PANIC();
69:         }
70: 
71:       g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth++;
72:       UP_DMB();
73:       bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_REENTER |
74:                              g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth);
75:       return true;
76:     }
77: 
78:   /* This is only a fast rejection.  The Peterson protocol below remains
79:    * authoritative while a new owner is between intent and owner publish.
80:    */
81: 
82:   if (g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner != 0)
83:     {
84:       bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_OWNER_BUSY |
85:                              g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner);
86:       return false;
87:     }
88: 
89:   /* Every attempt must publish a fresh intent and turn.  Leaving intent set
90:    * after a failed trylock makes the state stale and breaks trylock's
91:    * one-attempt contract.
92:    */
93: 
94:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[cpu] = 1;
95:   UP_DMB();
96:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.turn = other;
97:   UP_DMB();
98:   bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_INTENT);
99: 
100:   if (g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[other] != 0 &&
101:       g_bk7258_atomic_gate.turn == other)
102:     {
103:       g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[cpu] = 0;
104:       UP_DMB();
105:       __asm__ volatile("sev" ::: "memory");
106:       bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_CONFLICT);
107:       return false;
108:     }
109: 
110:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner = cpu + 1u;
111:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth = 1;
112:   UP_DMB();
113:   bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_ACQUIRED);
114:   return true;
115: }
116: 
117: static void bk7258_hwspinlock_relax(struct hwspinlock_dev_s *dev)
118: {
119:   (void)dev;
120:   __asm__ volatile("nop" ::: "memory");
121: }
122: 
123: static void bk7258_hwspinlock_unlock(struct hwspinlock_dev_s *dev)
124: {
125:   unsigned int cpu = (unsigned int)up_cpu_index();
126: 
127:   (void)dev;
128:   if (cpu >= 2 || g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner != cpu + 1u ||
129:       g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth == 0)
130:     {
131:       PANIC();
132:     }
133: 
134:   if (--g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth != 0)
135:     {
136:       UP_DMB();
137:       bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_UNLOCK |
138:                              g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth);
139:       return;
140:     }
141: 
142:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner = 0;
143:   UP_DMB();
144:   g_bk7258_atomic_gate.interested[cpu] = 0;
145:   UP_DSB();
146:   __asm__ volatile("sev" ::: "memory");
147:   bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_RELEASED);
148: }

154:   .unlock  = bk7258_hwspinlock_unlock

# Read-only design assessment

## Executive conclusion

The current BK7258 SMP IPI implementation has the right **software payload model**—per-target `pending` bits coalescing scheduler and SMP-call work—but the wrong **transport completion rule**:

- A sender that wins `g_ipi_kicked[cpu]` spins indefinitely until it can insert a raw mailbox descriptor.
- Replacing that spin with a bounded retry and returning an error would be unsafe: NuttX does not reliably retry either notification, and synchronous SMP calls may then wait forever.
- The safest minimal port-only design is to make `g_ipi_pending[target]` the authoritative **level condition**, make mailbox descriptors only advisory doorbells, and service the level condition on **every mailbox interrupt**, not only when a raw-kick descriptor is received.
- A sender should publish pending work, perform at most one mailbox enqueue attempt, and treat `-EAGAIN` as successful notification **only if the following hardware invariant is validated**:

> If the destination FIFO is full, it is non-empty and already supplies or retains a mailbox interrupt to the destination CPU; the destination mailbox ISR polls the shared pending level before returning.

This avoids both bounded dropping and unbounded spinning. It also handles the race where the FIFO fills between the status test and the TID commit.

If the BK7258 mailbox interrupt is not reliably level/re-pending while the FIFO is non-empty, this software construction is not sufficient. In that case, the production solution must use a dedicated hardware doorbell—preferably a validated AP-only route through MBOX1 or another documented cross-core interrupt source. Pure worker, idle, timer, or SEV retries are useful hardening but are not by themselves a complete IPI guarantee.

No files were modified.

# 1. NuttX architecture contract

## 1.1 `up_send_smp_sched()` is effectively required to succeed

The architecture declaration says that `up_send_smp_sched()`:

- is called to interrupt the target CPU and process delivered tasks;
- is called from a critical section;
- nominally returns zero or a negated errno.

Reference:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/include/nuttx/arch.h:2404-2423`

The relevant scheduler call site is more restrictive than the declaration suggests:

```c
per_cpu_var_smp(g_delivertasks, target_cpu) = priority;
up_send_smp_sched(target_cpu);
```

The return value is ignored:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/sched/sched.h:489-510`

Furthermore, a later delivery request is suppressed while `g_delivertasks[target]` already has the same pending value:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/sched/sched.h:495-509`

Therefore, if the architecture port:

1. leaves `g_delivertasks[target]` set,
2. fails to notify the target, and
3. returns an error,

the scheduler generally has no mechanism to recover. A bounded retry followed by `-ETIMEDOUT` is consequently a notification drop, even if a private BK7258 `pending` bit remains set.

The target must eventually call `nxsched_process_delivered()` in interrupt context:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/sched/sched_process_delivered.c:57-75`

It explicitly asserts interrupt context at line 68.

## 1.2 `up_send_smp_call()` has a stronger reliability requirement

NuttX first places call records on the target queues and then invokes the architecture hook:

- queue insertion:  
  `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/sched/sched_smp.c:473-483`
- architecture notification:  
  `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/sched/sched_smp.c:485`

`up_send_smp_call()` returns `void`:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/include/nuttx/arch.h:2426-2436`

The synchronous API then waits for every target completion:

- interrupt context: busy-waits on the semaphore count;
- thread context: waits uninterruptibly.

Reference:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/sched/sched_smp.c:312-369`
- especially `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/sched/sched_smp.c:339-359`

There is no timeout. Adding an architecture-local timeout would not be safe without changing the kernel because the queued call object and, in the default configuration, its cookie can be stack-backed. Returning while a target queue still references that object can create a use-after-return.

The current configuration does not define `CONFIG_SMP_CALL_POOL_COUNT`, so it defaults to zero:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/sched/sched_smp.c:44-46`

With that setting, the remote handler directly posts the original semaphore:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/sched/sched_smp.c:218-236`

If a nonzero call pool is enabled later, acknowledgements are themselves placed on the original CPU's SMP-call queue and `up_send_smp_call()` is invoked in the opposite direction:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/sched/sched_smp.c:230-234`

That makes a nonblocking, symmetric IPI path even more important.

## 1.3 Critical-section implications

The scheduler contract explicitly permits `up_send_smp_sched()` to be called with local interrupts disabled and scheduler/critical-section locks held. NuttX's SMP critical section uses a recursive spinlock plus local interrupt masking:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/include/nuttx/spinlock.h:1531-1534`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/irq/irq_csection.c:100-130`

Consequences:

- The port may not sleep or wait for a worker.
- It must not wait for a target action that may need a resource held by the caller.
- Long polling is unacceptable latency even if it eventually completes.
- Symmetric cross-core sends must not leave both CPUs spinning with interrupts masked.

# 2. Current BK7258 implementation

## 2.1 State machine

The current implementation has:

```c
static atomic_t g_ipi_pending[CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS];
static atomic_t g_ipi_kicked[CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS];
```

Reference:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_smpcall.c:38-39`

A sender:

1. ORs `SCHED` or `CALL` into `g_ipi_pending[target]`.
2. Claims `g_ipi_kicked[target]` with a zero-to-one compare/exchange.
3. If already kicked, returns success.
4. If it wins, repeatedly calls `bk7258_mbox_send()` forever on `-EAGAIN`.

Reference:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_smpcall.c:78-120`

The receiver:

1. exchanges its pending bits with zero;
2. runs the SMP-call handler and/or scheduler delivery handler;
3. clears `g_ipi_kicked[cpu]`;
4. if new pending bits appeared, sets `kicked` back to one and services them in the same ISR.

Reference:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_smpcall.c:122-189`

## 2.2 What is good about it

The pending bits are suitable for coalescing:

- `nxsched_smp_call_handler()` drains the target call queue, so one `CALL` bit can represent multiple queued calls.
- Scheduler delivery is itself represented by a per-CPU level-like `g_delivertasks` state.
- The receiver's clear/recheck sequence handles requests arriving while an IPI is being serviced.
- Redundant raw descriptors are harmless: a stale descriptor normally finds no pending bits and exits.

The AP RAM containing these objects is configured non-cacheable and inner-shareable:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_start.c:53-58`

This supports shared-state visibility, subject to the port's atomic and barrier implementation.

## 2.3 Fundamental weakness

`g_ipi_kicked[target] == 1` means:

> Some sender owns responsibility for eventually creating a hardware wakeup, or a previously created wakeup is still sufficient.

That promise is only kept because the owning sender spins until enqueue succeeds. If the loop is bounded, the promise can be broken.

On a non-`EAGAIN` error, the current implementation clears `kicked` but leaves `pending` set:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_smpcall.c:109-115`

For scheduler notifications this is unrecoverable through the normal NuttX call path because `g_delivertasks[target]` remains set and suppresses another call to `up_send_smp_sched()`.

For SMP calls, the current wrapper panics on an immediate error:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_smpcall.c:203-214`

That is preferable to silently returning, but the `-EAGAIN` path can never reach it because it spins indefinitely.

## 2.4 Why the unbounded loop is unsafe

`bk7258_mbox_send()` disables local interrupts around status checking and the three staging/commit writes:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mbox0.c:112-155`

The outer IPI caller may already be in a critical section. The unbounded loop therefore:

- holds whatever scheduler state led to `up_send_smp_sched()`;
- keeps revisiting MMIO with local interrupts unavailable;
- depends on the target draining a shared FIFO;
- can interact badly with simultaneous cross-core calls or callbacks that need reverse notification;
- has no failure diagnosis or progress deadline.

The vendor FreeRTOS port is not a sufficient model for NuttX reliability. Its analogous cross-core state coalesces commands with `crosscore_mb_busy`, but if busy it returns failure rather than guaranteeing delivery:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/os_source/freertos_smp_v2p0/FreeRTOS-Kernel/portable/GCC/ARM_CM33_NTZ/non_secure/port.c:1020-1052`

NuttX's synchronous SMP-call contract cannot tolerate that behavior.

The vendor SMP code uses `SEV` as a cross-core event wake mechanism:

The vendor register map exposes a second mailbox controller at `0x41020000`:

No active AP SMP implementation in the searched sources uses MBOX1 as an AP CPU1↔CPU2 doorbell. Its security ownership, endpoint mapping, interrupt source, and interaction with CP firmware are not established by the available code. It is a promising dedicated route but cannot safely be accessed without the BK7258 revision-specific TRM and CP firmware ownership confirmation.

# 4. Recommended minimal architecture-port design

## 4.1 Core idea

Use only one authoritative state:

```c
g_ipi_pending[target]
```

Remove `g_ipi_kicked` from the correctness protocol. A raw mailbox descriptor is merely a doorbell optimization. The pending bits are the request level.

Conceptual sender:

```c
old = atomic_or_release(&g_ipi_pending[target], requested_bits);

if (old == 0)
  {
    UP_DMB(); /* Pending data must precede status observation/doorbell. */

    ret = bk7258_mbox_send(target_physical_endpoint, raw_kick);

    if (ret == -EAGAIN)
      {
        /* Not a drop.  A full target FIFO is itself the target wake source. */
        ret = OK;
      }
    else if (ret < 0)
      {
        /* Programming, route, initialization, or hardware failure. */
        PANIC();
      }
  }

return OK;
```

Conceptual target-side service:

```c
bits = atomic_xchg_acquire(&g_ipi_pending[this_cpu()], 0);

if (bits & BK7258_IPI_CALL)
  {
    nxsched_smp_call_handler(irq, context, NULL);
  }

if (bits & BK7258_IPI_SCHED)
  {
    nxsched_process_delivered(this_cpu());
  }
```

The service routine must run:

1. at mailbox ISR entry;
2. after FIFO draining, before ISR return;
3. optionally when an explicit raw kick is decoded.

Running it at entry and tail is bounded: there is no transport spin. A stale raw descriptor is simply a no-op.

## 4.2 Why zero-to-nonzero detection is race-safe

`atomic_or_release()` returns the previous pending value.

There are two relevant orderings with the receiver's atomic exchange:

1. **Sender OR precedes receiver exchange.**  
   The receiver's exchange consumes the newly added bits. No new doorbell is required if an older request was already pending.

2. **Receiver exchange precedes sender OR.**  
   The sender observes an old value of zero and attempts a new doorbell.

This replaces the `pending/kicked` clear-and-rearm handshake with a simpler atomic level transition.

## 4.3 Why `-EAGAIN` is not a drop

The sender must publish the pending level and execute a DMB before reading destination FIFO state.

If the sender then observes the target FIFO as full:

- the target FIFO contains at least one descriptor;
- that descriptor has already asserted, or must retain/reassert, the target mailbox IRQ;
- the target mailbox ISR polls `g_ipi_pending[target]` irrespective of descriptor type;
- no additional raw descriptor is required.

The important race is:

1. sender publishes pending;
2. target concurrently drains;
3. sender tests full.

With correct device ordering:

- if the target drains and completes its ISR before the pending publication is visible, the subsequent status read should no longer report full and the sender can insert a raw kick;
- if the sender observes full, the target still has a mailbox interrupt path whose entry or tail occurs after the pending publication and consumes the shared level.

There is also a test/commit race in the current `bk7258_mbox_send()`:

1. status says not full;
2. another producer fills the destination FIFO;
3. TID commit encounters full.

The raw descriptor may be lost, but the pending level is not. The descriptor that made the FIFO full supplies the target interrupt, and the unconditional ISR poll services the IPI.

This proof depends on the hardware invariant stated in the executive conclusion. It must be verified against the TRM and on silicon.

## 4.4 Required files, without kernel changes

The minimal implementation belongs entirely in the custom architecture/board port:

1. `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_smpcall.c`
   - make pending authoritative;
   - remove correctness dependence on `g_ipi_kicked`;
   - perform one enqueue attempt;
   - treat only `-EAGAIN` as covered by the full-FIFO wake invariant;
   - fail-stop on other errors.

2. `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mbox0.c`
   - poll SMP pending at mailbox ISR entry and tail;
   - treat raw kick as a doorbell, not as the only reason to service pending;
   - keep ISR work bounded.

3. `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/include/bk7258_smp.h`
   - expose an ISR-only pending service helper if needed by mailbox and timer code.

No NuttX scheduler source needs to change.

# 5. Required invariants

The implementation is reliable only if all of these are maintained.

## I1. Pending is authoritative

If `g_ipi_pending[cpu] != 0`, work is owed to that CPU regardless of `g_ipi_kicked`, FIFO contents, or whether a raw descriptor exists.

No error path may clear pending work without executing it.

## I2. Publication precedes notification

For SMP calls, the queue insertion and all call data must be visible before the pending bit and doorbell.

For scheduler notifications, the `g_delivertasks[target]` write must be visible first.

Use release publication plus an explicit DMB before mailbox MMIO.

## I3. Every zero-to-nonzero transition establishes a wake condition

It must result in one of:

- a committed raw mailbox descriptor;
- observation of a full target FIFO whose interrupt is already a valid wake condition;
- a documented dedicated hardware level interrupt.

Returning `OK` without one of these is a drop.

## I4. Every mailbox IRQ polls pending

The target may not depend on seeing `BK7258_MBOX_RAW_KICK`. Any mailbox descriptor, write-full/error interrupt, or still-active FIFO condition must be enough to make the ISR inspect pending work.

## I5. Handler execution remains in IRQ context

`nxsched_process_delivered()` must not be called directly from a worker or idle thread. An idle fallback must self-pend a local IRQ and let the ISR invoke it.

## I6. Send-side execution is bounded

The architecture send hook must:

- publish;
- attempt at most one hardware commit;
- return.

It must not wait for FIFO space, a peer acknowledgement, a worker, or a remote state transition.

## I7. Hard errors are fail-stop

After NuttX has published scheduler or SMP-call work, errors such as:

- `-EINVAL`,
- `-EPERM`,
- mailbox not initialized,
- invalid endpoint,
- disabled or corrupted controller,

cannot be safely returned as normal transient failures. The port should record diagnostics and panic/reset rather than continue with an undeliverable scheduler state.

## I8. Boot reset is quiescent

The pending state may be cleared only while both CPUs are quiesced during controlled SMP startup/reset. The current boot preparation already initializes both arrays before secondary release:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_smpcall.c:217-231`

## I9. Shared memory remains coherent

The pending state must stay in non-cacheable/shareable AP RAM, or equivalent cache maintenance must be introduced on both CPUs.

## I10. CPU offline/hotplug is unsupported unless separately designed

A request to a powered-down or reset CPU cannot be recovered by this protocol. The existing port assumes two permanently online AP CPUs after startup.

# 6. Hardening and alternative mechanisms

## 6.1 CPU0 SysTick retry/poll hook

Only logical CPU0 owns SysTick:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_timerisr.c:76-103`

A board-port-only hardening option is:

- poll CPU0's own pending level from the CPU0 timer ISR;
- if CPU1 pending has remained nonzero, make one nonblocking raw-kick retry;
- track pending age and fail-stop if it exceeds a diagnostic threshold.

Advantages:

- guarantees periodic progress for CPU1→CPU0 requests even if their raw descriptor was lost;
- provides a watchdog for CPU0→CPU1;
- runs in valid IRQ context.

Limitations:

- CPU1 has no local SysTick;
- a retry timer is not a substitute for the full-FIFO wake proof;
- timer retries must never fill the FIFO with repeated redundant kicks.

This is recommended as diagnostic hardening, not as the primary correctness mechanism.

## 6.2 Idle retry

`up_idle()` can check whether local pending work exists. It must not call scheduler delivery directly; instead it can locally trigger the mailbox IRQ through STIR and then avoid entering WFI until the IRQ is observed.

It may also attempt one outbound retry if the opposite CPU has pending work.

Advantages:

- useful for CPU1, which has no SysTick;
- simple and board-local.

Limitations:

- no guarantee when the CPU is continuously busy;
- synchronous calls from interrupt context cannot rely on a worker or future idle period;
- idle polling alone does not provide prompt preemption.

Use only as a fallback.

## 6.3 Mailbox IRQ tail retry

At the end of any mailbox ISR, after locks associated with the logical transport have been released:

- service local pending;
- optionally make one outbound retry if a per-direction retry flag is set;
- never loop until success.

This is safe and useful because receipt of an opposite-direction message proves the peer is executing. It is still opportunistic unless combined with the full-FIFO level invariant or a periodic source.

## 6.4 Opposite-direction credit or drain epochs

Each CPU could increment a shared `drain_epoch[cpu]` whenever it removes entries from its receive FIFO. The sender can retry when it observes the destination epoch change.

A credit message is less attractive because the credit itself can encounter a full FIFO. Shared epochs avoid that recursion, but they still require a guaranteed sender-side execution hook—IRQ, timer, or idle—to observe the change.

This can reduce redundant retries but is more state than the minimal level design requires.

## 6.5 Dedicated retry worker

A dedicated high-priority worker is not suitable as the only IPI guarantee.

Constraints would have to include:

- one worker per sending CPU;
- worker created before any normal SMP-call use;
- fixed CPU affinity;
- no allocation;
- no semaphores or locks shared with target callbacks;
- one nonblocking MMIO attempt per activation;
- no dependency on an IPI to schedule the worker.

The existing mailbox worker is pinned to CPU0 and starts after SMP readiness:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:960-980`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1076-1145`

It therefore cannot provide symmetric early IPI progress. A worker also cannot rescue a synchronous SMP call made in interrupt context while the caller busy-waits.

Workers are acceptable for diagnostics or ordinary transport retries, not scheduler IPIs.

## 6.6 SEV/WFE

A possible supplementary scheme is:

1. publish pending;
2. execute `SEV`;
3. use a lost-event-safe WFE idle loop;
4. after wake, if pending is local, self-pend the local mailbox IRQ via STIR.

Risks:

- current idle is WFI;
- SEV does not produce IRQ context;
- a busy target does not trap merely because an event is set;
- cross-core event propagation and `RXEVT_SEL` behavior require silicon validation;
- replacing WFI with WFE requires careful event-register clearing to avoid either lost wakeups or a hot idle loop.

This is useful for idle wake latency and power, not as the sole scheduler IPI.

## 6.7 Write-full interrupt

The mailbox write-full status is an error indicating that software attempted to write a full FIFO. It is not a documented “space became available” interrupt:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/hal/mbox0_ll.h:520-529`

The current precheck normally avoids generating it. Intentionally writing into a full FIFO would lose that descriptor and can create an interrupt storm. Use write-full only for diagnostics and as another occasion to poll shared pending, not as a TX-ready event.

## 6.8 Reallocating MBOX0 FIFO slots

A dedicated reserved IPI slot would be attractive, but MBOX0 has only eight total entries and the current 2/3/3 partition is shared with CP traffic. A software reservation is reliable only if every possible writer, including CP firmware, observes the reservation. The AP port alone cannot enforce that for CPU0's receive channel.

Increasing FIFO depth may improve probability but does not establish correctness.

## 6.9 Dedicated MBOX1 or direct hardware route

This is the preferred fallback if the MBOX0 non-empty interrupt invariant cannot be proven.

A dedicated controller/channel would allow:

- one FIFO or level bit per direction;
- no contention with CP traffic;
- simple shared pending coalescing;
- bounded MMIO writes.

Before using MBOX1, verify:

- AP CPU1 and CPU2 access permissions;
- Secure/Non-secure aliasing;
- endpoint IDs;
- interrupt source and per-core routing;
- reset and clock ownership;
- whether CP or secure firmware already owns it;
- whether non-empty is a level interrupt.

Do not write system interrupt status registers or another CPU's assumed NVIC address without documentation. The available source proves only route-enable registers and a local NVIC STIR, not a remote software interrupt register.

# 7. Failure behavior

| Condition | Recommended behavior |
|---|---|
| Destination FIFO has space | Commit one raw kick and return `OK` |
| Destination FIFO reports full | Leave pending set; rely on target's already-active mailbox IRQ; return `OK` |
| FIFO becomes full between test and TID | Leave pending set; target services it from the interrupt generated by the descriptor(s) already in the FIFO |
| Duplicate/stale raw kick | ISR finds no pending bits; harmless no-op |
| Target interrupts temporarily masked | Pending remains; processing occurs after unmask and mailbox IRQ delivery |
| Mailbox logical transport is congested | Poll SMP pending at ISR entry before or independently of deferred logical descriptor processing |
| Invalid endpoint, uninitialized mailbox, permission error | Record state and panic/reset; do not return as if the scheduler can recover |
| Target CPU reset/offline | Fail-stop or platform recovery; never clear queued SMP calls and continue |
| Mailbox route/controller permanently broken | Pending-age watchdog should panic/reset; otherwise synchronous SMP calls necessarily hang |
| Continuous request stream | Coalesce through pending bits and queue draining; do not spin in sender or retry indefinitely inside one ISR |

A watchdog timeout may diagnose and reset the system, but it must not clear the request and continue. There is no safe local cancellation of a NuttX synchronous SMP call without kernel cooperation.

# 8. Main residual risks

1. **Mailbox interrupt semantics are not fully proved by source comments.**  
   The generated register definitions show FIFO non-empty and interrupt status but do not explicitly state all level/edge, mask, and re-pend behavior. This is the principal validation item.

2. **Shared MBOX0 contention with CP.**  
   CPU0's receive FIFO also handles CP traffic. The level-pending design tolerates full FIFO congestion for IPI liveness, but CP floods can increase ISR latency and starve ordinary mailbox descriptors.

3. **Descriptor processing can be deferred.**  
   CPU0 may stop popping when its software descriptor pool is full:

   - `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mbox0.c:277-283`

   Polling SMP pending at ISR entry ensures this does not also suppress IPIs.

4. **Atomic implementation is itself a progress dependency.**  
   This configuration uses a BK7258 software hardware-spinlock for libc atomics:

   - configuration:  
     `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/configs/nsh/defconfig:53`
   - atomic device:  
     `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_atomic.c:9-16`
   - Peterson-style implementation:  
     `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_hwspinlock.c:44-148`

   The atomic critical sections are short and run with interrupts disabled, but a failed or reset owner can still break progress. A single-writer generation-counter protocol could avoid atomic RMWs in this two-core system, at the cost of more complicated wrap and acknowledgement logic.

5. **SMP callbacks execute in mailbox IRQ context.**  
   This follows NuttX's design but means arbitrary SMP-call callbacks can extend mailbox IRQ latency. The port must not hold physical mailbox staging locks while executing callbacks.

6. **Future `CONFIG_SMP_CALL_POOL_COUNT > 0`.**  
   Reverse acknowledgement IPIs become active. The nonblocking level design supports this; the current unbounded send loop is especially risky in that configuration.

# 9. Validation required before claiming reliability

At minimum, test on the intended BK7258 revision:

1. Fill channel 1 and channel 2 to their configured depth and issue both scheduler and SMP-call requests without inserting a raw kick.
2. Verify that the target's existing mailbox IRQ services shared pending at ISR entry/tail.
3. Exercise the full-to-not-full race while publishing pending.
4. Force the FIFO to fill between status read and TID commit.
5. Run simultaneous CPU0→CPU1 and CPU1→CPU0 synchronous SMP calls.
6. Repeat with `CONFIG_SMP_CALL_POOL_COUNT > 0` to exercise reverse acknowledgements.
7. Mask the target mailbox IRQ, issue requests, then unmask and verify eventual service.
8. Flood CPU0 with CP descriptors until the software descriptor pool defers processing; verify SMP scheduling still progresses.
9. Stress repeated coalesced `SCHED` and `CALL` requests during target ISR entry and tail.
10. Disable the route intentionally and verify the pending-age watchdog produces a controlled panic/reset rather than silent continuation.
11. Confirm the mailbox interrupt remains pending or re-pends while receive FIFO data remains.
12. Confirm DMB plus the device status read provides the ordering used by the full-FIFO proof.

# Final recommendation

Implement the **shared pending level plus one-shot mailbox doorbell** in the BK7258 architecture port:

- no transport spin;
- no bounded drop;
- no correctness dependence on `g_ipi_kicked`;
- one nonblocking mailbox attempt on pending zero-to-nonzero;
- `-EAGAIN` accepted only under the validated full-FIFO-is-already-a-wake invariant;
- unconditional pending polling at mailbox ISR entry and tail;
- panic/reset on permanent send/configuration errors;
- optional CPU0 SysTick monitoring, idle self-pending, and one-shot retry hooks for diagnostics and extra resilience.

If the mailbox non-empty interrupt cannot be shown to retain/reassert reliably, do not attempt to manufacture reliability from workers or periodic retries. Validate and dedicate MBOX1 or another documented AP cross-core interrupt route instead.
